content: Certainly. 1. The Pricing Index Model for Medicare Part B Drugs was published by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services in 2018, detailing its implementation and implications in the Federal Registry (Volume 83, Issue 210, Pages 54546–61). 2. Fontrier AM, Gill J, and Kanavos P explored the international effects of external reference pricing and its relevance for national policymakers in the European Journal of Health Economics, emphasizing its potential impact on healthcare systems. 3. Vogler S, Lepuschütz L, Schneider P, and Stühlinger V conducted a study on cross-country coordination in pharmaceutical pricing, presenting their findings in a comprehensive final report. 4. Espin J, Rovira J, and Labrie AO examined pharmaceutical pricing policies and interventions, contributing to the broader understanding of medicine pricing, availability, and affordability. 5. Kanavos P, Fontrier AM, Gill J, and Efthymiadou O analyzed whether external reference pricing achieves its intended outcomes, providing evidence of its national-level impact in the European Journal of Health Economics. 6. Leopold C, Mantel-Teeuwisse AK, Seyfang L, Vogler S, de Joncheere K, Laing RO, et al. investigated the influence of external price referencing on medicine prices across 14 European countries, highlighting significant price variations. 7. Maniadakis N, Kourlaba G, Shen J, and Holtorf A developed a taxonomy of pharmaceutical policies and examined global trends, correlating them with country income levels in BMC Health Services Research. 8. Hasan SS, Kow CS, Dawoud D, Mohamed O, Baines D, and Babar ZUD reviewed pharmaceutical policy reforms in the Asia-Pacific region, focusing on drug price regulation in countries such as Australia, China, India, Malaysia, New Zealand, and South Korea. 9. Adriaen M, De Witte K, and Simoens S analyzed pricing strategies for originator and generic medicines post-patent expiry in Belgium, providing insights into market dynamics. 10. Brekke KR, Grasdal AL, and Holmås TH compared reference pricing and price cap regulation in the pharmaceutical sector, discussing their implications for drug pricing and market behavior. 11. Brekke KR, Canta C, and Straume OR investigated whether reference pricing discourages generic competition in pharmaceutical markets, using evidence from policy reforms. 12. Ghislandi S, Armeni P, and Jommi C assessed the long-term impact of generic reference pricing in Italy, focusing on its effects over a decade. 13. Grootendorst P and Stewart D re-evaluated the impact of reference pricing on antihypertensive drug expenditures in British Columbia, providing a detailed economic analysis. 14. Hsiao FY, Tsai YW, and Huang WF studied the effects of price regulation, market entry, and information shocks on Taiwan's pharmaceutical market between 2001 and 2004. 15. Kaiser U, Mendez SJ, Rønde T, and Ullrich H examined the outcomes of reference price reforms on pharmaceutical pricing in Denmark, offering evidence-based insights. 16. Koskinen H, Ahola E, Saastamoinen LK, Mikkola H, and Martikainen JE evaluated the impact of reference pricing and generic substitution on the daily cost of antipsychotic medications in Finland. 17. Moreno-Torres I, Puig-Junoy J, and Raya JM analyzed the effects of repeated cost-containment policies on pharmaceutical expenditures in Spain, highlighting their economic implications. 18. Puig-Junoy J investigated the impact of generic reference pricing interventions in the statin market, providing a detailed policy evaluation. 19. Bergman MA, Granlund D, and Rudholm N assessed the consequences of reforms in the Swedish pharmaceutical market, focusing on costs per defined daily dose. 20. Kwon HY, Bae S, Choi S, Park S, Lee EK, Park SM, et al. studied the effects of significant drug price cuts on expenditures and utilization of antihypertensive drugs in Korea. 21. Lee IH, Bloor K, Hewitt C, and Maynard A evaluated the effects of new pricing and copayment schemes for pharmaceuticals in South Korea, analyzing their economic and healthcare outcomes. 22. Suh HS, Kim JA, and Lee IH examined the impact of a price cut reform on the cost and utilization of antidiabetic drugs in Korea, using national health insurance data. 23. Yoo KB, Lee SG, Park S, Kim TH, Ahn J, Cho MH, et al. analyzed the effects of drug price reductions and prescribing restrictions on antihypertensive drug expenditures and utilization in Korea. 24. Johnson JT, Neill KK, and Davis DA conducted a five-year study on the outcomes of benefit design changes, including reference pricing for proton pump inhibitors, within a state employee health plan. 25. Stargardt T, Schreyögg J, and Busse R explored the effects of fixed drug pricing in Germany, focusing on group formation, price calculation, and their broader implications. 26. Marđetko N and Kos M evaluated the introduction of therapeutic reference pricing in Slovenia and its economic consequences. 27. Stargardt T assessed the impact of reference pricing on switching behavior and healthcare utilization in the statin market in Germany. 28. Armeni P, Jommi C, and Otto M analyzed the simultaneous effects of pharmaceutical policies from the perspectives of payers and patients, using Italy as a case study. 29. Schneeweiss S, Dormuth C, Grootendorst P, Soumerai SB, and Maclure M evaluated the net health plan savings from reference pricing for angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors in elderly British Columbia residents. 30. Andersson K, Petzold MG, Sonesson C, Lönnroth K, and Carlsten A investigated the effects of policy changes in Sweden's pharmaceutical reimbursement schedule on drug expenditures. 31. Leopold C, Zhang F, Mantel-Teeuwisse AK, Vogler S, Valkova S, Ross-Degnan D, et al. studied the impact of pharmaceutical policy interventions on antipsychotic medicine utilization in Finland and Portugal during economic recessions. 32. von der Schulenburg F, Vandoros S, and Kanavos P reviewed the effects of drug market regulation on pharmaceutical prices in Europe, focusing on ACE inhibitors. 33. Grootendorst PV, Marshall JK, Holbrook AM, Dolovich LR, O’Brien BJ, and Levy AR analyzed the impact of reference pricing for nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents on analgesic drug use and costs. 34. The WHO Collaborating Centre for Pharmaceutical Pricing and Reimbursement Policies provided a comprehensive overview of pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement policies across 47 countries. 35. Cheng W, Fang Y, Fan D, Sun J, Shi X, and Li J studied the effects of the zero mark-up policy on medicines in Beijing community health facilities. 36. Fu H, Li L, and Yip W examined the intended and unintended impacts of price changes for drugs and medical services in China. 37. Yang C, Shen Q, Cai W, Zhu W, Li Z, Wu L, et al. analyzed the impact of the zero-markup drug policy on hospitalization expenditures in rural China. 38. Zhou Z, Su Y, Campbell B, Zhou Z, Gao J, Yu Q, et al. evaluated the financial impact of the Zero-Markup Policy for Essential Drugs on patients in county hospitals in rural China. 39. Li L, Chen Y, Yao L, and Li Y assessed the effects of implementing the Zero-Markup policy in community health service institutions in Chengdu. 40. Bhaskarabhatla A, Chatterjee C, Anurag P, and Pennings E studied the regulatory impact of partial price controls on metformin in India. 41. Lu CY, Ross-Degnan D, Stephens P, Liu B, and Wagner AK analyzed changes in antidiabetic medication use following price regulations in China. 42. Chu HL, Liu SZ, and Romeis JC assessed the effects of drug price reduction policies on older populations in Taiwan. 43. The Seventy-Second World Health Assembly emphasized improving transparency in markets for medicines, vaccines, and other health products. 44. Kohler JC, Mitsakakis N, Saadat F, Byng D, and Martinez MG examined the role of pharmaceutical pricing transparency in Brazil’s public procurement system. 45. Moodley R and Suleman F evaluated the impact of South Africa’s single exit price policy on originator and generic medicines using time series analysis. 46. The Australian Government Department of Health outlined procedural and operational guidelines for pharmaceutical benefit scheme price disclosure arrangements. 47. Pauwels K, Huys I, Vogler S, Casteels M, and Simoens S reviewed managed entry agreements for oncology drugs in Europe, providing lessons for future policy development. 48. Langley T, Lacey J, Johnson A, Newman C, Subramanian D, Khare M, et al. evaluated a price transparency intervention for commonly prescribed medications and its effect on institutional expenditures. 49. Berdud M, Chalkidou K, Dean E, Ferraro J, Garrison L, Nemzoff C, et al. discussed the future of global health procurement, focusing on pricing transparency issues. 50. Moon S advocated for increased transparency in medicine pricing to address global healthcare challenges.
